{{Tennis tournaments}}
[[Tennis]] was part of the [[Summer Olympic Games]] program from the inaugural [[1896 Summer Olympics]], but was dropped after the [[1924 Summer Olympics]] due to disputes between the [[International Tennis Federation|International Lawn Tennis Federation]] and the [[International Olympic Committee]] over how to define amateur players.<ref>{{cite web | author=Soltis, Greg | date=July 27, 2012 | url=https://www.livescience.com/2782-olympic-events-history.html | title=Olympic Events Through History | publisher=[[LiveScience]] | access-date=2012-08-01}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | author=Williams, Wythe | date=July 27, 1928 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1928/07/27/archives/soccer-and-tennis-barred-in-olympics-international-body-by-1614.html | title=SOCCER AND TENNIS BARRED IN OLYMPICS | work=[[The New York Times]] | access-date=2012-08-01}}</ref> After two appearances as a [[demonstration sport]] in 1968 and 1984 (with a U-21 age limit),<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.itftennis.com/olympics/history/history/overview.aspx | title=Olympic Tennis Event – History: Overview | publisher=[[International Tennis Federation]] | access-date=2012-08-01}}</ref> it returned as a full medal sport at the [[1988 Summer Olympics]] open for all players regardless of their age and status and has been played at every summer Games since then.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1981/10/02/sports/2-more-olympic-games.html | title=2 More Olympic Games | work=[[The New York Times]] | date=October 2, 1981 | access-date=2012-08-01}}</ref>

==Medals==
In 1896, 1900, 1904, 1988, 1992, semifinal losers shared bronze medals. In all other years, a playoff match for the bronze medal was staged. The Olympic tournaments have increased in perceived importance since their reintroduction, with some players, critics and sports pundits considering winning gold at the Olympics just as prestigious as winning a major title and some considering it even more prestigious.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.letsecondserve.com/2012/07/olympics-or-slams-whats-more-important.html|title=Olympics or Slams – What's More Important For Tennis Players? |publisher=Let, Second Serve|date=July 12, 2012|access-date=April 5, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.worldtennismagazine.com/archives/8213|title=How Important Is an Olympic Gold Medal in Tennis?|author=Paul Fein|publisher=World Tennis Magazine|date=September 20, 2012|access-date=October 29, 2013|archive-date=September 24, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170924061839/http://www.worldtennismagazine.com/archives/8213|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

[[File:TENFEM WR 01.08.21-3244.jpg|thumb|right|[[Laura Pigossi]] and [[Luisa Stefani]] from Brazil, winners of the women’s doubles bronze medal at the [[Tennis at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's doubles|2020 Summer Olympic Games]]]]

[[File:Ukraine at the 2020 Summer Olympics016.jpg | thumb | right | Ukraine's [[Elina Svitolina]] with her bronze Olympic medal ]]

===Gold medal records===
Both [[Serena Williams|Serena]] and [[Venus Williams]] have each won a record four gold medals, three each as a doubles pairing, the only players to win the same Olympic event on three occasions. Venus Williams (four gold, one silver) and [[Kathleen McKane Godfree]] (one gold, two silvers, and two bronzes) are the all-time record holders for the most Olympic tennis medals, with five each. [[Andy Murray]] is the only player to have won two singles gold medals, and the only singles player to have retained the Olympic title. [[Nicolás Massú]], Venus Williams, and Serena Williams are the only players in the [[Open Era]] to win both the singles and same-sex doubles tournaments at one Games, doing so in [[Tennis at the 2004 Summer Olympics|2004]], [[Tennis at the 2000 Summer Olympics|2000]], and [[Tennis at the 2012 Summer Olympics|2012]] respectively.

===Golden Slams===
A player who wins an Olympic or [[Paralympic Games|Paralympic]] gold medal and all four majors in the same year is said to have won a [[Grand Slam (tennis)#Golden Slam|Golden Slam]], while a player that has won all four Grand Slam titles and Olympic gold during their career has a 'career Golden Slam'. As of 2026, [[Steffi Graf]] (in 1988) is the only player to have won a single-year Golden Slam. [[Gigi Fernandez]], [[Serena Williams]] and [[Venus Williams]] are the only players to complete career Golden Slam in doubles twice. In men's tennis, [[Andre Agassi]], [[Rafael Nadal]] and [[Novak Djokovic]] each won career Golden Slams. Multiple doubles players have achieved the feat, with Serena Williams the only player to complete the career Golden Slam in both singles and doubles.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Tignor|first1=Steve|title=1988: Steffi Graf wins the Golden Slam|url=https://www.tennis.com/pro-game/2015/07/1988-steffi-graf-wins-golden-slam/55786/|access-date=17 September 2017|publisher=[[Tennis (magazine)|Tennis.com]]|date=30 July 2015}}</ref> In 2021, wheelchair tennis players [[Diede de Groot]] and [[Dylan Alcott]] achieved the equivalent wheelchair tennis prize with Paralympic gold, with Alcott additionally completing the single-year Golden Slam.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dylan Alcott achieves history-making 'golden slam' with US Open final victory |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2021/sep/13/dylan-alcott-achieves-history-making-golden-slam-with-us-open-final-victory|access-date=28 September 2021|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=13 September 2021}}</ref>

===Tiebreaker games===
[[File:Victoria Azarenka, Serena Williams and Maria Sharapova with medals 2012.jpg|right|thumb|2012 Women's Singles medalists, [[Serena Williams]] (center), [[Maria Sharapova]] (right) and [[Victoria Azarenka]] (left)]]
Since 2021, the deciding set (third) has a 7-point [[tiebreaker]] game to decide the match at 6-all. Should the tiebreaker game be tied at 6-all, whoever first establishes a clear two point lead wins the set and the match.

==Surface==
The playing surface of the court varies between Olympic Games. It has been on [[hard court]] for every Olympics since 1984 except for the [[Tennis at the 1992 Summer Olympics|1992]] and [[Tennis at the 2024 Summer Olympics|2024 Olympics]] (which were on a [[clay court]]) and the [[Tennis at the 2012 Summer Olympics|2012 Olympics]] (which was played on a [[grass court]]). 

The [[Tennis at the 1908 Summer Olympics|1908]] and the [[Tennis at the 1920 Summer Olympics|1920]] editions of the Olympics were the two other instances that tennis was played on grass courts. 

The [[Tennis at the 1908 Summer Olympics|1908]] and [[Tennis at the 1912 Summer Olympics|1912]] editions of the Olympic games were the only instances that indoor tennis competitions were contested alongside the outdoor ones, but since then it has only been outdoor. Those indoor competitions were also the only instances that [[Wood court|wooden surfaces]] were used for tennis at the Olympics. 

From the [[Tennis at the 1896 Summer Olympics|1896]] until the [[Tennis at the 1904 Summer Olympics|1904]] editions of the Olympics, tennis was contested on clay courts. Clay courts were in use again for the [[Tennis at the 1912 Summer Olympics|1912]], [[Tennis at the 1924 Summer Olympics|1924]] and at the [[Tennis at the 1968 Summer Olympics|1968]] editions of the Olympics, but would only be used again at the [[Tennis at the 1992 Summer Olympics|1992]] Olympics.

The changing playing surface gives certain players different advantages and disadvantages not seen in most other Olympic sports. On three occasions, the event has been held, wholly or partly, at a Grand Slam venue - twice at the [[All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club|All-England Tennis Club]] at Wimbledon (1908 and 2012) and once at [[Stade Roland Garros|Roland Garros]] in Paris (2024).

==Point distribution==
From the [[2004 Summer Olympics|2004]] until the [[2012 Summer Olympics]], the [[Association of Tennis Professionals|ATP]] and the [[Women's Tennis Association|WTA]] Tours awarded ranking points, for singles players only, who competed at the Summer Olympics. This was discontinued beginning with the [[2016 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.itftennis.com/news/79975.aspx|access-date=1 February 2015|title=ITF and ATP announce Olympic agreement|publisher=ITF Tennis |date=1 Jun 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150202074534/http://www.itftennis.com/news/79975.aspx |archive-date= Feb 2, 2015 }}</ref><ref name="ATP tour">{{cite web|url=http://nanjing.itftennis.com/olympics/players/ranking-points.aspx|access-date=16 September 2014|title=Ranking Points|publisher=ITF Tennis |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140921182754/http://nanjing.itftennis.com/olympics/players/ranking-points.aspx |archive-date= Sep 21, 2014 }}</ref>
